messages:
noah: hey all, day 2 here. building runtime and linking fails with weird device symbol errors when I add a new .cu file. any ideas?

noah: build/link error:
```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/src/gpu/kernel_launcher.o: in function `launchKernel':
kernel_launcher.cu:(.text+0x2f): undefined reference to `__device_stub__Z12my_kernelPi'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

noah: I compiled with cmake (out-of-source): `cmake .. && make -j16`. nvcc picks up /usr/local/cuda. nvcc --version shows 12.1. building on Ubuntu 22.04, gcc-11.

mika: welcome! that __device_stub__ undefined ref usually means CUDA device code wasn't linked into the final binary (separable compilation/relocatable device code issue). are you compiling .cu with nvcc and linking with nvcc or g++?

noah: our top-level CMake creates targets with `set_source_files_properties(... PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)` and links everything with standard C++ linker, not using nvcc for final link.

samir: yep, if you have device functions across translation units you need relocatable device code (RDC). Two fixes: 1) enable relocatable device code so nvcc emits device stubs: add `-DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS=--relocatable-device-code=true` or in modern CMake `-DCMAKE_CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION=ON`, and make sure linking is done via nvcc (CMake does this when it knows a target is CUDA). 2) Alternatively, put kernel launchers in same TU as device code to avoid RDC.

natanael: also check CMake 3.18+ macros: `set_target_properties(mytarget PROPERTIES CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION ON)` is preferred per-target. And ensure you link against CUDA::cudadevrt if using device linking: `target_link_libraries(mytarget PRIVATE CUDA::cudart_static CUDA::cudadevrt)` depending on static/shared choices.

noah: tried `-DCMAKE_CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION=ON` and rebuilt. linker still complains but different symbol: `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterLinkedBinary_` at link time.

rosie: that second error usually happens when you don't link cudadevrt or you mix static/shared cudadll selections. If you enable separable compilation you need to link cudadevrt to handle device linking, or let nvcc do the link which pulls it in. In our CMake we add `if(CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER) target_link_libraries(mytarget PRIVATE CUDA::cudart)` and set `CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION ON` per-target.

buildbot: dev-image note: the redwood/dev-runtime images include a working CMake toolchain and a sample config for CUDA separable compilation. Try `docker run -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/dev-runtime:2025-06 bash` and run `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION=ON`.

noah: ok i set `set_target_properties(runtime PROPERTIES CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION ON)` and also added `target_link_libraries(runtime PRIVATE CUDA::cudart_static CUDA::cudadevrt)` per natanael. rebuilt with clean out-of-source and now link succeeds. unit GPU smoke passes.

mika: nice! could you add a short note in onboarding about RDC and when to use it? It's a recurring gotcha for new runtime devs.

noah: will do and add sample CMake snippet. thanks all :raised_hands:

noah: closing thread.
